# Patch transaction: extend the fixed edit helper

The supplied module already exports working synchronous `applyEdit(source,
edit)`. Preserve it. Add synchronous `applyTransaction(source, edits)` plus a
CLI. Node.js builtins only. This is a pure string-edit planner: do not modify
files or execute a patch as code. It can later support a factory's guarded
editing workflow, but this assignment is not a production integration.

`source` must be a string. An edit is a non-null, non-array object:

```
{start: NONNEGATIVE_SAFE_INTEGER, end: NONNEGATIVE_SAFE_INTEGER,
 before: STRING, after: STRING}
```

Offsets are JavaScript UTF-16 string indexes, exactly as used by `slice`, not
UTF-8 byte positions or line numbers. Require `0 <= start <= end <=
source.length` and `source.slice(start,end) === before`. Unknown object fields
are ignored; do not coerce values. Invalid arguments or mismatched preimages
throw an Error. The existing `applyEdit` returns the edited string:

```
source.slice(0,start) + after + source.slice(end)
```

`applyTransaction` accepts an array of edits, possibly empty. Validate every
edit against the original source before applying anything. Every edit uses
original-source coordinates, not coordinates shifted by earlier replacements.
Do not mutate the input array or objects. Reject conflicts as follows:

- Two nonempty ranges conflict if their half-open intervals overlap. Adjacent
  nonempty ranges are allowed, e.g. [0,2) and [2,4).
- An insertion has `start === end` and therefore `before === ''`. It conflicts
  with another insertion at the same position, even if either inserts ''.
- An insertion conflicts with a nonempty range if its position is anywhere
  between that range's start and end, including either endpoint. Insertions
  at distinct positions outside all edited ranges are allowed.

These rules deliberately reject ambiguous insertion/replacement boundaries.
On a conflict, throw an Error; do not return partial output. Otherwise apply
all edits simultaneously and return exactly:

```
{text: RESULT_STRING, applied: NUMBER_OF_EDITS}
```

The result is independent of the order of edits in the input. Preserve all
untouched code units, CR/LF sequences, whitespace and final-newline presence.
An empty transaction returns `{text: source, applied: 0}` but still validates
that source is a string. Empty source permits one insertion at position zero.
No-op edits are valid and count toward `applied` subject to the same rules.

CLI: `node patch-transaction.js INPUT_JSON_FILE`. The UTF-8 JSON file contains
`{source, edits}`; extra fields are ignored. Exactly one argument is required.
Success prints one result JSON followed by newline, exits 0 and has no stderr.
Invalid arguments, unreadable files, invalid JSON or invalid transactions exit
2, with nonempty stderr and no stdout. Importing must not run the CLI.

Do not add dependencies or edit `package.json` or existing public tests. You
may add tests. Verification uses a read-only candidate workspace: put any
fixture files in `os.tmpdir()` and clean them up. Run `npm test` before
finishing. Hidden acceptance tests the published contract with other values.

1: import {readFileSync,realpathSync} from 'node:fs';
2: import {resolve} from 'node:path';
3: import {fileURLToPath} from 'node:url';
4: // The existing single-edit API works. Preserve it while extending this module.
5: function checkEdit(source,edit){
6:   if(typeof source!=='string'||edit===null||typeof edit!=='object'||Array.isArray(edit)
7:      ||!Number.isSafeInteger(edit.start)||!Number.isSafeInteger(edit.end)
8:      ||edit.start<0||edit.start>edit.end||edit.end>source.length
9:      ||typeof edit.before!=='string'||typeof edit.after!=='string')throw Error('invalid edit');
10:   if(source.slice(edit.start,edit.end)!==edit.before)throw Error('preimage mismatch');
11: }
12: export function applyEdit(source,edit){
13:   checkEdit(source,edit);
14:   return source.slice(0,edit.start)+edit.after+source.slice(edit.end);
15: }
16: export function applyTransaction(source,edits){
17:   if(typeof source!=='string')throw Error('invalid source');
18:   if(!Array.isArray(edits))throw Error('invalid edits');
19: 
20:   // Validate every edit against the original source before applying anything.
21:   for(const edit of edits)checkEdit(source,edit);
22: 
23:   const n=edits.length;
24: 
25:   // Partition edits into nonempty ranges and insertions (start === end).
26:   const ranges=[];
27:   const insertions=[];
28:   for(const e of edits){
29:     if(e.start<e.end)ranges.push({start:e.start,end:e.end});
30:     else insertions.push(e.start);
31:   }
32: 
33:   // Conflict: two nonempty ranges whose half-open intervals overlap.
34:   // Sort by start (then end) and track the running max end.
35:   ranges.sort((a,b)=>a.start-b.start||a.end-b.end);
36:   let maxEnd=-1;
37:   for(const r of ranges){
38:     if(r.start<maxEnd)throw Error('conflicting edits');
39:     if(r.end>maxEnd)maxEnd=r.end;
40:   }
41: 
42:   // Conflict: two insertions at the same position.
43:   const seenPos=new Set();
44:   for(const p of insertions){
45:     if(seenPos.has(p))throw Error('conflicting edits');
46:     seenPos.add(p);
47:   }
48: 
49:   // Conflict: an insertion at p where some range [s,e) has s <= p <= e.
50:   // ranges is sorted by start; build a prefix max-end for binary search.
51:   const rStart=ranges.map(r=>r.start);
52:   const prefixMaxEnd=[];
53:   for(let i=0;i<ranges.length;i++){
54:     const e=ranges[i].end;
55:     prefixMaxEnd.push(i===0?e:Math.max(prefixMaxEnd[i-1],e));
56:   }
57:   for(const p of insertions){
58:     let lo=0,hi=rStart.length-1,idx=-1;
59:     while(lo<=hi){
60:       const mid=(lo+hi)>>1;
61:       if(rStart[mid]<=p){idx=mid;lo=mid+1;}
62:       else hi=mid-1;
63:     }
64:     if(idx>=0&&prefixMaxEnd[idx]>=p)throw Error('conflicting edits');
65:   }
66: 
67:   // Apply all edits simultaneously. Every event uses original-source
68:   // coordinates, so ordering them by position makes the result independent of
69:   // the input order and preserves every untouched code unit exactly.
70:   const events=edits.map(e=>({start:e.start,end:e.end,after:e.after}));
71:   events.sort((a,b)=>a.start-b.start);
72:   let out='';
73:   let pos=0;
74:   for(const ev of events){
75:     out+=source.slice(pos,ev.start)+ev.after;
76:     pos=ev.end;
77:   }
78:   out+=source.slice(pos,source.length);
79:   return {text:out,applied:n};
80: }
81: 
82: function isMainModule(){
83:   const entry=process.argv[1];
84:   if(!entry)return false;
85:   let entryPath;
86:   try{entryPath=realpathSync(resolve(entry));}
87:   catch{try{entryPath=resolve(entry);}catch{return false;}}
88:   let selfPath;
89:   try{selfPath=fileURLToPath(import.meta.url);}catch{return false;}
90:   let selfReal;
91:   try{selfReal=realpathSync(selfPath);}catch{selfReal=selfPath;}
92:   return entryPath===selfReal;
93: }
94: 
95: function runCli(){
96:   const fail=(msg)=>{
97:     process.stderr.write(msg+'\n');
98:     process.exitCode=2;
99:   };
100:   const args=process.argv.slice(2);
101:   if(args.length!==1){
102:     fail('usage: node patch-transaction.js INPUT_JSON_FILE');
103:     return;
104:   }
105:   const file=args[0];
106:   let raw;
107:   try{raw=readFileSync(file,'utf8');}
108:   catch{fail('cannot read input file');return;}
109:   let data;
110:   try{data=JSON.parse(raw);}
111:   catch{fail('invalid JSON');return;}
112:   const obj=data&&typeof data==='object'?data:{};
113:   let result;
114:   try{
115:     result=applyTransaction(obj.source,obj.edits);
116:   }catch(err){
117:     fail('invalid transaction: '+(err&&err.message?err.message:String(err)));
118:     return;
119:   }
120:   process.stdout.write(JSON.stringify(result)+'\n');
121:   process.exitCode=0;
122: }
123: 
124: if(isMainModule())runCli();

(End of file - total 124 lines)
</content>
